findings.description: mark_invalid writes {"kind":"invalid","id":...} to the day file of served_at. If the impression was served in a different timezone or its served_at is naive/aware inconsistently, the date may differ from the one used at append, so the marker lands in a different file and for_day never sees it. Refunds then silently have no effect. Also, repeated refunds are not idempotent in the file, though harmless on read.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the same day derivation is used for append and mark_invalid (e.g. normalise to UTC), and consider validating that the original record exists.
findings.title: Invalid marker is keyed only by impression id and lacks campaign

findings.description: The pacer previously kept in-memory spend. Now can_bid calls spend(), which calls for_day, which re-reads and JSON-parses the entire day file, for each campaign on each bid request (eligible loops over all campaigns). Cost is O(requests x campaigns x impressions in the day), growing through the day; the report does the same per campaign. This will become very slow on the hot bid path.
findings.suggestion: Cache per-day, per-campaign spend in memory (updated on record/refund) or index the log; avoid re-reading the file on each bid.
findings.title: Whole day file re-read and parsed for every campaign on every bid

findings.description: Impressions are bucketed by impression.served_at.hour, while the cap check uses now.hour from request.received_at. If the datetimes carry different tzinfo (or one is naive), buckets mismatch and the hourly cap is applied to the wrong hour. Also day files are chosen by served_at.date() in its own timezone.
findings.suggestion: Normalise all datetimes to one timezone before deriving date and hour.
findings.title: Hourly bucket uses impression's own timezone hour, not the request's
